title: P.E.I. horse makes harness racing history with 29 straight wins
summary: A Prince Edward Island horse has made harness racing history, winning her 29th consecutive race Thursday night to set a modern-day North American pacing record.

image.caption: Earl Watts, trainer of Windemere Skye, says the filly will have the winter off and return to race next summer. (CBC)

blocks.text: A Prince Edward Island horse has made harness racing history, winning her 29th consecutive race Thursday night to set a modern-day North American pacing record.
3-year-old filly breaks modern-day North American pacing record in Charlottetown
The three-year-old filly Windemere Skye took the lead early at Red Shores in Charlottetown and held on for the win. She remains undefeated in all 29 races of her career.
Her trainer, Earl Watts, said he was still taking it all in after the race.
“Unreal. It’s hard to believe we just set a record,” Watts said.
The previous record of 28 consecutive wins was first set by Cam Fella in 1983 and matched by Firms Phantom in 2001, according to Lee Drake, Red Shores’ manager of racing and broadcast.
Windemere Skye, with Marc Campbell in the driver's seat, at Red Shores in Charlottetown on Thursday night. (CBC)
Watts called Windemere Skye “a very special filly” and credited driver Marc Campbell and the team caring for her at the farm.
“You won’t get too many like her. In my lifetime, you won’t get another one,” he said.
The record-breaking win came against a field of older mares. Drake had said before the race that the competition would be strong, and Watts said he was nervous going in.
“I had faith in her,” Watts said. “But no, I’m glad it’s over.”
Watts said the plan is to give Windemere Skye the winter off before bringing her back to race next summer.
Thinh Nguyen is a digital reporter with CBC P.E.I. He can be reached at thinh.duc.nguyen@cbc.ca
